Native source-ordered mixed-effects and wild-bootstrap audit frames

etr_native_source_audit_frames.Rd

Six Python-independent, read-only native R adapters for realized participant and nested-trial functional random effects, whole-participant and nested-trial bootstrap identity audits, FPCA wild-bootstrap truncation scans, and target-specific truncation selections. No model fitting, automatic tuning, bootstrap resampling, or statistical qualification is performed.

Usage

etr_functional_random_effect_frame(result, effect = "intercept")
etr_functional_trial_random_effect_frame(result)
etr_functional_mixed_effects_full_refit_audit_frame(bootstrap)
etr_functional_mixed_effects_full_refit_trial_audit_frame(bootstrap)
etr_fpca_wild_bootstrap_truncation_scan_frame(result)
etr_fpca_wild_bootstrap_truncation_selection_frame(result)

Arguments

result

Native named record of already-realized mixed-effects functions or FPCA truncation scan/selection outputs. Source-required numerical fields and matrix dimensions are validated.

effect

Participant-level random functional intercept or slope.

bootstrap

Native named record of full-refit source and bootstrap participant or trial identity histories.

Details

Frozen source: published eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0, commit c1cd95ad718327550f7e55393ff38582872f7a94, including functional_mixed_effects.py, functional_mixed_effects_nested.py, functional_mixed_effects_full_refit.py, and wild_selection.py. Candidate-major and participant-major row ordering, zero-based source/bootstrap indices, and missing selection components are retained. Python dataclass and pandas return types are not reproduced and remain an explicit unresolved source-contract gap. For full-refit trial audits, pass the generated native refit object directly or provide the equivalent four-identifier rows per replicate. Repeated draws of a source participant receive distinct bootstrap participant and trial identifiers. For the participant random-effect and nested-trial effect frames, callers may now also pass the corresponding native joint B-spline Gaussian mixed fit records directly. Their fitted random-effect functions are adapted without any statistical refit, preserving source-order rows and the prior named-list interface. The result is still an R data frame, not a Python pandas frame or a certified Python result-type contract.

Value

Native R data frame, one row per source-defined audit unit. The functions never invoke the Python runtime.
